title: An inverted yoke for touch and mouse: drag down to pull up
dek: The on-screen yoke now works like a real control column: drag down to pull the nose up, drag up to push it down, with touch or a mouse.
description: Fly Kai Tak's on-screen yoke is now inverted for touch and mouse: drag down to pull the nose up, drag up to push it down, matching the keyboard.
hero_alt: The 747 on the IGS approach, with the round on-screen yoke in the bottom left corner.
hero_caption: The on-screen yoke, bottom left, works with touch or a mouse.
card_sub: Drag down to pull up, with touch or mouse

title: Share Fly Kai Tak posts on Threads
dek: Every blog post now has a Threads share button alongside X, Facebook, Reddit, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, email and copy link.
description: Fly Kai Tak blog posts can now be shared on Threads with one click, with the title and link pre-filled.
hero_alt: The Bank of China Tower and the Central skyline in Fly Kai Tak.
hero_caption: Found a view you like? Share the post it came from.
card_sub: A new share button on every post

title: Landmarks tour, plus Ocean Park and Happy Valley
dek: From the Bank of China Tower to the Garden Hill beacon: the landmarks you can spot around Kai Tak, and two new additions, Ocean Park and Happy Valley Racecourse.
description: A tour of the Hong Kong landmarks in Fly Kai Tak, with screenshots, plus the new Ocean Park amusement park and Happy Valley Racecourse.
hero_alt: The Bank of China Tower's braced, faceted shaft among the Central towers.
hero_caption: The Bank of China Tower and the Central skyline.
card_sub: Plus Ocean Park and Happy Valley

title: Flying Kai Tak on your phone: landscape, a cleaner toolbar and bigger controls
dek: A one-row toolbar with a More drawer, touch controls sized for short landscape screens, and a prompt that asks portrait players to turn the phone sideways.
description: Fly Kai Tak on mobile: a compact toolbar with a More drawer, landscape touch controls, a rotate prompt for portrait, full screen on Begin descent and safe-area support.
hero_alt: A 747-400 on the IGS approach in a landscape phone window, with the yoke bottom left and gear, flaps and thrust lever bottom right.
hero_caption: The IGS approach on a phone-sized landscape screen: a one-row toolbar, the yoke on the left and the gear, flaps and thrust lever on the right.
card_title: Fly Kai Tak on your phone
card_sub: Landscape, a cleaner toolbar, bigger controls

title: The checkerboard turn: flying the IGS 13 approach
dek: Descend over Tsing Yi, aim at a checkerboard on a hill in Kowloon, then turn a 747 right by 47° over the rooftops. How the Runway 13 approach works in Fly Kai Tak.
description: How the famous Runway 13 IGS approach into Kai Tak works in Fly Kai Tak: the 088° course, the checkerboard on the hill, the 47° right turn over Kowloon City and the landing grade.
hero_alt: Cockpit view of a 747 banking right over Kowloon City with Kai Tak's Runway 13 and the harbour ahead.
hero_caption: Mid-turn in the 747-400. The heading has swung from 088° to 102°, the artificial horizon is banked, and Runway 13 is in sight beyond the sports ground.

title: Real Hong Kong: building 1998 from open data
dek: The coastline, roads and about 24,000 buildings under the Kai Tak approach come from official Hong Kong open data. Here is what is real, and what we changed to make it 1998.
description: How Fly Kai Tak builds Hong Kong from Lands Department open data and SRTM terrain, and the 1998 corrections: no Kai Tak redevelopment, no West Kowloon buildings, and the Walled City as an option.
hero_alt: A 747 on the apron at Kai Tak with the runway running out into Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline behind.
hero_caption: Spectator mode from the car park roof: the apron, Runway 13 running into the harbour, and the skyline across the water.

title: Typhoons, fog and city lights: weather and night at Kai Tak
dek: Six weather presets, a lightning toggle, gusts that push the aircraft around and a night mode that lights up Kowloon. The same approach, very different flights.
description: Weather and night flying in Fly Kai Tak: clear, rain, typhoon, storm, low cloud and fog presets, wind gusts and turbulence, lightning, and a lit-up Kowloon at night.
hero_alt: Cockpit view of a 777 on the IGS approach in a typhoon, with heavy rain and the city fading into grey.
hero_caption: The 777-200 on the IGS in a typhoon. The ATC call quotes the live QNH, and the wind readout shows 36 knots gusting 52.
